root_idea.summary: Making something firm, compact, and well-ordered through binding, weaving, or closely arranged extension.
root_idea.development: The root develops from securing or compacting a thing to well-woven forms, well-knit bodies, waist-binding, and ordered tracks or patterns such as those associated with the sky.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quranic plural حُبُك is retained as the public citation form because the evidence directly supports this lexical plural and the QAC occurrence is its definite genitive form.

senses.definition: Paths, tracks, or ordered streaks, especially the courses of stars, the Milky Way, or streaks of cloud in the sky.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression وَالسَّمَاءِ ذَاتِ الْحُبُكِ, the term may denote visible heavenly paths or patterns. The Quran-focused interpretation also allows these paths to be understood as intelligible orders perceived through reflection, not only as physical tracks.

senses.definition: Beautifully ordered structure or construction, specifically the well-formed constitution of the heavens.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an alternative Quranic interpretation of ذَاتِ الْحُبُكِ, emphasizing the heavens' beautiful, firmly ordered construction rather than their visible tracks.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind or tie; to make fast, firm, compact, or well-finished; to weave a material firmly and well.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of cloth and other things; the result may be described as well-made or beautiful in its workmanship.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike, cut, or sever with a sword.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested of striking the middle or waist, cutting flesh above the bone, severing the neck, and cutting a structure such as a grape-vine trellis.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To sew together the leaves of a book or bind a book.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later or current usage recorded as an extension of binding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make a knot firm or fast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Form II usage centered on securing a knot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To stripe or weave with stripes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a striped or stripe-woven garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind oneself with a waistband or gird oneself by raising or tucking up one's clothes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of securing clothing around the waist; the source's example involving a woman does not impose a gender restriction on the construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bind or tuck up the waist-wrapper and thereby gird oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A clothing construction associated with اِحْتِبَاءٌ; the lexical discussion records a distinction between this form and related forms of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A waistband or the binding part of a waist-wrapper; also the folded portion let down from it for carrying something, or a cord or garment used to bind the waist.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may refer either to the tied part of the garment or to the cord or garment performing the binding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thong joining the head of a camel saddle to its supporting pieces.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the corresponding fastening in saddles such as the قَتَب or رَحْل.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To prepare oneself to depart or to devote oneself exclusively and diligently to an affair.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative idiom based on fastening the waistband.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An enclosure for cattle made from reeds or pieces of wood placed crosswise and tied together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term denotes the bound construction itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The selvages or border threads of a garment or piece of felt.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the black threads sewn along the borders or extremities of the material.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A streak, line, ripple, or patterned row in a surface or material.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of ridges or ripples in sand and water, wavy forms in crisp hair, streaks in a helmet or mountain, and rows or scales in a coat of mail. The specifically Quranic heavenly applications are represented under the Quranic senses above.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The blackness of the area above a pigeon's wings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized lexical use for this marked area of the bird.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Firmly or well bound, woven, or made; well-finished and beautiful in workmanship.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to cloth and, in one usage, to a bow-string.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sewer of book leaves, a bookbinder, an ornamental sewer, or a maker of ribbon-like lace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later or current occupational usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Striped or patterned; of hair, crimped or marked with rippled forms.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a garment and of hair whose texture appears wavy or streaked.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Well-knit, firm, or compact in bodily make; strong and well-built.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a horse or other beast, including one with an even, high back and rump.

cautions: Lane records several variant readings for the Quranic expression; the displayed headword follows the QAC lemma حُبُك, while the supplied occurrence is its definite genitive form حُبُكِ. The Quranic interpretation correspondingly includes both heavenly pathways or patterns and beautiful construction.
